knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says the costs and income are divided by billable hours to get the base rate, so the work that can be billed recovers them. Using all paid hours, a listing average or a wished-for rate does not do this.
The lesson says travel, set-up and clean-down time does not shrink with the length of the service, so a minimum charge covers the visit. It does not replace a written quote for every booking.
The lesson says to use your own costs and billable hours, checked against local evidence. A single vendor's price list, a friend's rate or a listing-site price is not a sound check on its own.

practicalCriteria: Learner calculates billable hours from a one-month log, showing each non-billable deduction.
Learner builds a base rate from a worksheet of annual costs and an income target, showing the calculation.
Learner sets a minimum charge for a short job and writes the wording the client will see before the visit.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 1 is not done: Estimate paid hours in a year, then subtract travel, admin, marketing, training and leave to find billable hours.
